clue.text: Bag and barrel overturned in fight

indicators.note: in places the turned barrel word inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a ruck is a scrap or brawl, also a scrum-like melee in rugby

indicators.note: overturned says the word for a barrel is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a cask is a barrel

explanation.surface: A bag and a barrel get knocked over during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' looks like a verb beside 'fight', but it is the noun defined; a ruck is also the loose scrum in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back by hikers.

clue.text: Plain nasty

explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unattractive in looks, while nasty means unpleasant or threatening, as a situation can turn ugly.

clue.text: Floor made of rock in enclosure

indicators.note: in places the rock word within the word for an enclosure

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A floor laid with stone inside a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level, or floor, of a building.

clue.text: List of names including commercial vehicle

indicators.note: including means the list word holds the commercial word inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, as for duties
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A register of names that lists a commercial van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' looks like the adjective in 'commercial vehicle', but it is the noun, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater car, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Ways on island accepted by average islander

indicators.note: accepted by means the ways-plus-island group is taken inside the word for average

parts.note: the mean is the average
lanes are ways or roads

explanation.surface: Roads on an island are welcomed by a typical inhabitant.
explanation.walkthrough: Melanesia is the island group of the western Pacific, so 'islander' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Melanesian is a native of Melanesia, the Pacific island group including Fiji and Vanuatu.

clue.text: Getting information in crib, what you'll write is convincing

indicators.note: in places the information word within the word for a crib

parts.note: a cot is a baby's crib
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Getting the facts from a crib sheet makes your written answer persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' and 'what you'll write is' only join the pieces to the definition; a crib sheet is the surface's red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is persuasive and clear.

clue.text: Metal casks containing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Metal casks containing (8)' is cut short: TUNS containing G plus TEN needs words for G and TEN that the held clue lacks, and no reprint found.

clue.text: Relation should be excited when capturing record

indicators.note: capturing means the jumbled word takes the record word inside it
excited suggests agitation, so the letters of when are stirred up

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A relative ought to get excited on catching a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of 'when' is split open by the record, so the record sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, a family relation.

clue.text: Cat, previously without name, linked with group

indicators.note: without says the name letter is taken out of the word for previously

parts.note: once means previously, formerly
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A cat, formerly nameless, joins up with a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked with' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocelot is a spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Fine wine? There's no time for it

indicators.note: There's no time means the time letter is dropped from the wine word

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A good wine, but nobody has time to drink it.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or all right, like fine.

clue.text: Said to be holding assistance back? That'll be denied

indicators.note: holding means the said-to-be word contains the reversed assistance word

parts.note: reputed means said or believed to be

indicators.note: back says the assistance word is turned round

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: Someone said to be withholding help: that claim will be rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That'll be' links the wordplay to the definition 'denied'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or disown, so a claim repudiated has been denied.

clue.text: Still fast, even though boxed in

indicators.note: boxed in means the even-though word is enclosed by the word for fast

parts.note: pacy means fast, quick
if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant if dull'

explanation.surface: Remaining fast even when hemmed in, like a boxer on the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a verb, to calm, not the adverb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To still someone is to calm or soothe them.

clue.text: Interested in country accent

parts.note: into means keen on or interested in, as 'into jazz'
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a country's way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice, a kind of accent or manner of speaking.

clue.text: Request admittance needing to take food inside

indicators.note: take food inside means the eating word goes within the admittance word

parts.note: entry is admittance
eats or eat is food, informally

explanation.surface: Asking to be let in because one needs a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to take' only sets up the container signal 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal.

clue.text: Some think it's challenging

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Some think it's challenging (6)': the hidden KITSCH is there but no word defines it (kitsch is tawdry, not challenging), so the clue looks cut short; no reprint found.

clue.text: Speed with which famous person has got book out

indicators.note: has got book out means the book letter is removed from the famous person word

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: How quickly a star managed to get a book published.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness, a literary word for speed.

clue.text: Approval shown by muster behind party's leader

indicators.note: behind places the muster word after the party letter
the leader of party is its opening letter

parts.note: to raise an army is to muster it

explanation.surface: Approval signalled by rallying behind the party chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts RAISE after P, the first letter of 'party's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is commendation, expressed approval.

clue.text: See responses given by voters coming out when this survey's published?

definitions.text: See responses given by voters coming out when this survey's published?

parts.words: See responses given by voters coming out when this survey's published?
parts.note: a survey taken of voters as they leave the polling station, published on election night

explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll asks people leaving a polling station how they voted.

clue.text: Man on earth upset Greek god

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the earth word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: soil is earth

explanation.surface: A fellow on the ground knocked over a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SOIL into LIOS, below HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Helios was the sun god of Greek myth.

clue.text: US vice-president mostly required to suppress material Insect identified by chap before it's metamorphosed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'US vice-president mostly required to suppress material Insect identified by chap before it's metamorphosed (8)' has 22-across's clue merged into it, and CHEN(ILL)E needs a word for ILL that 'required' cannot give; no reprint found.
annotationWithheld.clue: US vice-president mostly required to suppress material Insect identified by chap before it's metamorphosed

clue.text: Interval indicated by author is amended, or cut out

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
or cut out means those two letters are removed from author is

explanation.surface: A pause shown by a writer who is corrected, or edited out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' removes OR from AUTHORIS to leave AUTHIS, which 'amended' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or pause, an interval in continuity.

clue.text: Insect identified by chap before it's metamorphosed

indicators.note: before places the chap word ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: a man is a chap

indicators.note: metamorphosed means transformed, so the letters of it's change order

explanation.surface: An insect recognised by a man before it changed form.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal suits the surface, since insects undergo metamorphosis.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis is a predatory insect, often called the praying mantis.

clue.text: Getting up in public I'd embarrassed powerful family

indicators.note: Getting up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit within the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rising in public, I was embarrassed by a mighty dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Getting up' reads the run publIC I'D Embarrassed from the bottom; 'in' is the hiding signal, added to the checked draft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the ruling banking dynasty of Renaissance Florence.

clue.text: Time consumed by wrongful act in crazy plan

indicators.note: in places the combined piece within the word for crazy

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: consumed by means the time word is swallowed by the wrongful act word

parts.note: a sin is a wrongful act
a term is a period of time, as a school term

explanation.surface: An hour wasted on misbehaviour as part of a mad scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Time here is a period, not the usual single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mastermind something is to plan and direct it.

clue.text: Page with work by English poet

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A page beside an English work by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an English poet of the 18th century.

clue.text: Top dog, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the dog's name is heard, not seen

parts.note: a Peke is a Pekinese, a small dog

explanation.surface: The best dog, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' turns PEKE into a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is a summit, the highest point.

clue.text: Objection about second person in purchase of company?

indicators.note: about means the objection word goes round the second-person word

parts.note: but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Raising an objection over someone during a company takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyout is the acquisition of a controlling share in a business.

clue.text: Friendly note, by telegram, one received

parts.note: so, or soh, is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: received means the telegram word takes in the one

parts.note: a cable is a telegram
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cordial note sent by telegram, one that arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only joins the note to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable means companionable, enjoying others' company.
